dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: What to do...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: It's just... My daughter Ellin has her heart set on joining the Knights of Favonius; she's training for the tryouts now.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: *sigh* I had really hoped to help mentor her, but she just doesn't believe me when I say I used to be an adventurer. She just wants to train alone.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: There's nothing I can do to prove it to her, either... Once you've got a wife and kids, it'd be selfish and reckless to carry on going out on these dangerous adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: My responsibility to care for my family takes priority over the ego boost I'd get from going on an adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: I'm still an adventurer at heart though, and I certainly still know a thing or two about it.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Once when I was on an adventure, I noticed these wooden dummies that the hilichurls use for combat training.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: They look pretty sturdy — I'm sure they'd be great for Ellin to train with, too.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Could you go and collect a few hilichurl training dummies for me? Of course, I respect the adventurers' code and wouldn't make you do it for nothing. How about it?

response.speaker: Herman
response.text: That's the spirit! Ah, I was just like you back when I first joined the Guild, up for anything! And when I say anything...

response.speaker: Herman
response.text: Ahem. Just joking of course! Off you go now.

choices.text: They're only hilichurls, you can take 'em...

response.speaker: Herman
response.text: I really can't. Even adventurers have their limitations; there's only so much adventure you can take on in one go.

response.speaker: Herman
response.text: And the adventure that is married life is more than enough to deal with on its own, I don't care who you are...

response.speaker: Herman
response.text: So if you please... I will leave the hilichurls to you.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Did you find some training dummies?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Ooh, nice... Yes, these are nice and sturdy!

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: If they can withstand a pummeling by a hilichurl, they should be able to take whatever Ellin throws at them.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Thank you! And as per the adventurers' code, here's your reward.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Hmm, now what's the best way to train...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: I'm practicing for the Knights of Favonius' tryouts. But I just can't get the hang of it and I don't have anyone to teach me.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: My dad keeps offering to be my mentor; he says he used to be an adventurer... Yeah, right!

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: There's no way someone like my dad is going to help me get through the Knights of Favonius tryouts.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Then he said he was gonna get me some sort of training equipment. I can't imagine what on earth he has in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Did you find some training dummies?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, however...

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Whew... Looks like you put too much force into it. I don't know how you managed to break such a sturdy wooden contraption though.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: I suppose no one pulls their punches on account of a few wooden sticks in the heat of battle...

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: I can't give this to Ellin as-is. But it's good wood, so with a bit of work it should be fine!

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: I've assembled it, albeit with some difficulty — it's not half bad, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: All thanks to you, ultimately. Here's your payment. As promised, I don't take favors for free.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: You can quit being an adventurer, but you can't quit respecting the code!

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Wow, this wooden dummy is actually pretty good. This'll make training much easier.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Where on earth my dad got such a sturdy training dummy from is beyond me.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Surely he can't have bought it? This would have been so expensive...

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Did you find some wooden dummies?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: Ellin's busy training away, and this is the one thing I can do for her...

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: If I was still an adventurer I'd do it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: And what with the current state of Mondstadt's Adventurers' Guild, most of my former co-adventurers have also given up the trade.

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: There's not much that can be done about it. The Knights of Favonius are the influential ones these days, all the young people want to join up. By contrast, the idea of enduring the harsh world of the wild alone, as an adventurer...

dialogues.speaker: Herman
dialogues.text: It doesn't really appeal to anyone anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Huh... So this is the training equipment my dad promised to get me.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: I feel like it'll fall apart if I so much as touch it.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: But it's better than nothing. I'll make use of it.
